text_blocks.snippet: Thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome (TTS), also known as vaccine-induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia (VITT), is characterized by blood clots (thrombosis) and a low platelet count (thrombocytopenia). Common symptoms include severe headache, blurred vision, difficulty speaking, drowsiness, seizures or confusion, difficulty breathing, chest pain, leg swelling, and persistent abdominal pain. Bruising and pinpoint rash-like spots (petechiae) may also occur due to low platelets, according to the National Institutes of Health (NIH).
